content.text:
NASA Eyes Bulk Rocket Buy for Moon Base Amid SpaceX Phaseout: The visible opening says NASA is close to announcing bulk rocket launches for its roughly $30 billion Moon Base effort, amid high launch demand and supply constraints, and begins a quote from Moon Base lead Carlos García-Galán. The page truncates at the start of the quote; the available evidence does not establish a completed purchase or identify suppliers, order value, launch count, or windows. (time=2026-10-06T12:00:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
NASA Unveils Plan to Establish America’s First Moon Base: NASA’s plan describes up to 25 Phase 1 missions, including 21 landings, through 2029; up to 60 tons of cargo over up to 24 landings in 2029–2032; and procuring dozens of commercial launches per year through the Launch Services Program. (time=2026-03-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

These findings concern lunar lander delivery execution, not the reported bulk rocket purchase. (time=2026-05-18; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
